title: Pontotoc County retailers accounted for one in nine private jobs last December
excerpt: Going into Small Business Saturday, federal payroll records show 1,134 retail jobs last December, up 20 from the same month a year earlier.

paragraphs.text: Retailers in Pontotoc County carried 1,134 jobs on their payrolls last December, about one in nine of the county’s private-sector jobs. As shoppers head into Small Business Saturday on Nov. 28, federal employment records show how much work the retail trade accounted for during the last holiday season.

The local retail job count barely moved between October and November 2025. It went from 1,127 to 1,123, then climbed by 11 in December. The same months a year earlier had 1,108, 1,112 and 1,114 jobs. That left December 2025 with 20 more retail jobs than December 2024.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 107 private retail establishments in the county in the final quarter of 2025, one more than a year earlier. Average weekly pay across those retail jobs rose from $562 to $628 over the same period. The figures cover retail workplaces of all sizes, including chains. They do not give a separate count of independently owned shops.

Retail payrolls stayed close to the December level in January, when the county recorded 1,132 jobs. They fell to 1,110 in February and reached 1,121 in March. These are counts of jobs at Pontotoc County workplaces. They give readers a baseline for the shopping season, but do not measure sales or how many workers stores hired for this November.
